title: AJK Election Process Concludes: PML-N Wins 25 Seats, PPP 12, After Bagh Re-Polling
detail: Azad Jammu & Kashmir's drawn-out 2026 Legislative Assembly election process concluded on August 15, 2026 with the announcement of results for the last two contested Bagh constituencies following re-polling at stations ordered after irregularities. PPP's Sardar Zia-ul-Qamar defeated PML-N's Mushtaq Minhas in LA-15 (Central Bagh) by 1,891 votes, while PML-N's Sardar Mir Akbar Khan won LA-16 (Eastern Bagh) by 3,833 votes. With the full count in, PML-N finishes as the largest party with 25 of the assembly's directly elected seats (and is expected to add roughly 6 more via reserved seats for women, technocrats, overseas Kashmiris, and Ulema-o-Mashaikh), placing it in a strong position to form the next AJK government; PPP takes 12 seats. The election — held in three staggered phases since late July under the shadow of the JAAC reserved-seat protest movement, which JKHRO says has killed at least 89 people since June — was the most violence-marred AJK poll in years, with 7 of 11 Poonch-division constituencies forced to postpone voting during the August 10 third phase.

media.caption: PML-N emerges as the largest party in the AJK Legislative Assembly with 25 seats as the drawn-out 2026 election process concludes

title: J&K's 80th Independence Day Passes Off Peacefully Under Multi-Layered Security Grid
detail: Jammu & Kashmir marked India's 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026 without incident, despite the Intelligence Bureau's August 11 warning of a possible ISI-backed infiltration or terror plot timed to the holiday. Chief Minister Omar Abdullah hoisted the national flag at the main J&K function at Srinagar's Bakshi Stadium, which was ringed by sharpshooters, drone and CCTV surveillance with facial recognition, quick-reaction teams, and bomb-disposal units; checking and frisking were intensified region-wide, including along the LOC and International Border in Jammu, Samba, Rajouri, and Poonch, and in North Kashmir's Uri, Keran, Tangdar, and Gurez sectors. J&K IGP V.K. Birdi said 'August 15 is the people's function; the role of the police and security agencies is to organise and secure the celebrations.' Thousands attended flag-hoisting ceremonies at district and block levels across the Valley with no reported security incidents.

media.caption: Parade at Bakshi Stadium, Srinagar as J&K marks the 80th Independence Day under tight multi-layered security, Aug 15, 2026
